ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a speed-time curve, with the vertical axis as Speed (RPM) and the horizontal axis as Time (sec). The speed first remains at 1000 rpm, then after t = 4 s begins to rise linearly, reaches 1500 rpm at t = 8 s, and thereafter remains at 1500 rpm. Therefore, the speed-change segment that needs to be calculated is from 4 s to 8 s, lasting 4 s, with the speed linearly rising from 1000 rpm to 1500 rpm. Reasoning: Convert the mechanical rotational speed into angular velocity, taking 1 rpm = 2π/60 ≈ 0.1047 rad/s. Initial speed ω1 = 1000 × 0.1047 = 104.7 rad/s; final speed ω2 = 1500 × 0.1047 = 157.05 rad/s. During the linear acceleration period, the average angular velocity is (ω1 + ω2)/2 = 130.875 rad/s, so the angular displacement θ = 130.875 × 4 = 523.5 rad. The load torque is 2 Nm, and the load work W_load = T_L θ = 2 × 523.5 = 1047 J. The moment of inertia J = 0.1 kg·m², and the increase in rotational kinetic energy ΔE_k = 0.5 J (ω2² - ω1²) = 0.5 × 0.1 × (157.05² - 104.7²) ≈ 685.1 J. Ignoring motor losses, the energy consumed by the motor during the speed-change period is the load work plus the increase in kinetic energy: E = 1047 + 685.1 ≈ 1732.1 J, rounded to about 1732 J.

method.method_draft: Inspect the figure to identify only the ramp segment from 4 s to 8 s, where speed changes linearly from 1000 rpm to 1500 rpm. Convert the initial and final mechanical speeds to rad/s. Compute the angular displacement during the ramp using the average speed from the trapezoidal area under the speed-time curve. Then compute load work T_L theta using the 2 Nm load torque, and add the increase in stored rotational kinetic energy using J = 0.1 kg·m^2. Since losses are neglected, this sum is the motor energy consumed during the speed change.

planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Apply rotational work-energy: with losses neglected, motor energy during acceleration equals work against load plus change in kinetic energy, E = T_L theta + (1/2)J(omega_2^2 - omega_1^2). method.method_draft: From the figure, take the ramp duration as 4 s and compute the angular acceleration from the speed slope, after converting 1000 rpm and 1500 rpm to rad/s. Use the text-given load torque and inertia to find the motor torque required during the ramp: load torque plus accelerating torque J alpha. Because the speed ramp is linear, this torque is constant. The resulting energy is the required consumed energy because motor losses are neglected.

图像描述：图中是速度-时间曲线，纵轴为 Speed (RPM)，横轴为 Time (sec)。曲线在 t=4 s 前保持 1000 rpm；从 t=4 s 到 t=8 s 直线升高到 1500 rpm；之后保持 1500 rpm。因此速度变化段是 4 s 到 8 s，持续 4 s，且为线性斜坡。

planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use the rotational equation of motion during acceleration: T_motor = T_load + J alpha. Since alpha is constant from the linear ramp, motor torque is constant. Then integrate mechanical power P = T_motor omega(t): E = integral P dt = (T_load + J alpha) integral omega dt. Convert rpm to rad/s; alpha = (omega_2 - omega_1)/4 and integral omega dt = ((omega_1 + omega_2)/2)*4. Numerically this is approximately 1732 J under the expected rounding convention.
